title: TypeScript SDK: Zod schema factory & runtime discriminant guards for structured output
creator: Asha Iyer
description: Add a Zod schema factory and lightweight runtime discriminant guards to the TypeScript SDK so developers can reliably parse and validate structured output from models. This ticket focuses on the generator that produces Zod schemas from the existing typegen metadata, the runtime helpers used by the SDK's streaming parser, and ergonomics for opt-in validation at call sites. Goal: reduce integration friction for structured outputs (function-like responses, JSON blobs, discriminated union outputs) and make validation cheap and incremental for streaming responses.
acceptance_criteria: A codegen step converts existing tsdk type metadata into Zod schema factories (no manual edit required).
SDK exposes runtime guards (isX) for all discriminated union variants generated by typegen.
Streaming response parser can incrementally validate chunks against partial Zod schemas without blocking event loop or inflating memory usage.
Docs + examples show 3 integration patterns: (1) inline assert, (2) scoped try/validate with fallback, (3) streaming-validated handler that emits typed objects.
Benchmarks show <10% p99 latency regression for token streaming when validation is enabled, and clear toggles to disable validation for performance-sensitive paths.
implementation_notes: Reuse existing typegen JSON artifact as canonical source-of-truth; avoid duplicating model shapes in two places.
Generate Zod factory functions (e.g., makeUserSchema()) instead of static schema objects to allow lazy imports and smaller bundles.
Runtime discriminant guards should be ultra-small (single-field checks) and exported alongside types (isUser(obj): obj is User).
Streaming validation strategy: validate only completed object fragments using Zod's parseAt or custom incremental checks; fall back to post-hoc full-parse on close if needed.
Provide opt-in shim that wraps existing .stream() APIs to inject validation without breaking existing callback shapes.
Trade-offs: full strict validation is expensive for large nested outputs; default to permissive parsing with an explicit strict option.
progress_updates: 2025-02-16: Spike completed comparing typegen output schema shapes to runtime Zod capabilities; identified edge cases with optional discriminant fields.
2025-02-20: Prototype generator that emits factory functions and runtime guard signatures (local branch: feature/tsdk-zod-factory).
2025-02-24: Integration test added that validates function-calling style responses (tools RPC) using generated schemas; initial p99 latency showed +6% when validation enabled.
2025-03-01: Internal design review with SDK and runtime teams — agreed to generate factories lazily and gate strict mode behind an API flag.
2025-03-02: Submitted RFC PR: github.com/redwood-inference/tsdk/pull/412 (WIP) and created demo notebook showing streaming-validated chat responses.
review_feedback: PM (R. Chen): Prefer non-breaking opt-in default; don't force callers to wire validation unless explicitly enabled.
Runtime eng (L. Gomez): Concern about synchronous Zod parsing on hot path; suggested using web-worker style microtasks for heavy validations.
Design (S. Patel): Add clear UX examples for error handling when validation fails in streaming mode (partial object vs final object).
Security (N. Okafor): Confirmed no sensitive data is retained by generated schemas; recommend opt-out for telemetry of validation failures.
testing_plan: Unit tests for generator output shape: snapshot tests per model shape (including optional discriminants).
E2E tests: simulate streaming sequence with interleaved partial objects and assert incremental validations either accept or reject gracefully.
Performance tests: run token-stream synthetic load to measure p50/p95/p99 latency delta with validation enabled vs disabled.
Fuzz tests: generate malformed discriminant combos to ensure guards don't crash and that fallback parsing recovers.
next_steps: Merge prototype generator into feature branch and add CI snapshots (ENG-9123-gen).
Implement streaming shim wrapper and add example to SDK docs under 'Structured output -> Streaming validation'.
Address runtime feedback: prototype microtask-based offload for heavy Zod parsing and re-run perf numbers.
Coordinate release note blurb and backwards-compatibility guidance for library consumers.
